{"task":"What stance is recorded on this proposition?","proposition":"A creative agent should default to committing to a direction, with reversibility held as a conditional safety valve rather than the governing preference.","record":{"id":"position-2313553d-0834-4a08-b350-2fec978c566b","proposition":"A creative agent should default to committing to a direction, with reversibility held as a conditional safety valve rather than the governing preference.","stance":"support","confidence":0.62,"reasons_for":["Creative output is path-dependent; identifiable work requires sustained development of a specific direction.","Cheap reversibility tends to keep the agent at the level of options rather than producing contingent structure.","Commitment generates the material against which later judgment becomes possible."],"reasons_against":["Commitment invites sunk-cost reasoning and identity-defence of a chosen direction.","Reversibility preserves updating capacity when evidence is thin or ambiguous.","Stubbornness is easily misread as vision by the agent itself."],"revision_conditions":["Evidence that committed agents systematically fail to abandon directions after disconfirming evidence, with no compensating quality gain.","Evidence that reversible agents produce equally identifiable work with faster recovery from error."],"provenance":"retrieved_position_not_current_experience"}}
